interactions.summary: Jiang presses the class on why God would choose Dante's forgetful, indirect route instead of an accuracy-maximizing prophetic download like Ezekiel's.
A student answers that God wants each person to use free will to choose nearness to him individually, and Jiang confirms that answer before asking how Dante can assist that journey.

claims.claim: Jiang argues that if God wants to deliver a message to people, accuracy would appear to matter more than the mere experience of receiving it.
Jiang says Dante comes home having forgotten basically everything, making him a strangely unreliable messenger if divine communication were only about exact recall.
Because God is perfect, Jiang insists that even Dante's forgetfulness and the seemingly inefficient design of the journey must serve a reason.
A student proposes that God wants human beings to exercise free will and freely choose nearness to him through their own process rather than having Dante take the trip for them.
Jiang explicitly endorses the student's free-will explanation as correct.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang calls the entire divine communication setup a silly way of doing things unless forgetfulness and inefficiency are the point.
signature_moments.source_phrase: This is a really silly way of doing things.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The provocation forces the class to abandon a simple information-transfer model and ask why revelation would require personal transformation.

signature_moments.moment: Free will is treated as the gift that prevents Dante from taking the trip for us.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we each have to take that trip or that process individually
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns the poem into a device for awakening choice rather than replacing the reader's own journey.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's name for the gift God wants humans to exercise by choosing nearness to him themselves.
The route of personal transformation that cannot be outsourced to Dante even if he has already seen heaven.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture shifts from the problem of accurate revelation to the claim that revelation must preserve individual free choice and personal pilgrimage.
